custody.registrar: Aporia -- registers anchors; outside the producing cell
custody.form: append-only out-of-repository store on M1 (SKULLPORT) in the MWO-0004 D2-1 form: one row per registered record = {registered_at_utc, registrar, record_kind, repo_path, blob_sha256, commit_sha}; identifiers and hashes only, no content
custody.store_access: read through the comms connection (EW_DB_HOST=192.168.1.202 off M1): `python -m ops.custody.registry read [--kind K] [--json]`; verify: `python -m ops.custody.registry verify` (exit 0 ok, 1 chain break -> custody ROW_CHAIN_BROKEN, 3 unreachable -> STORE_UNREACHABLE; neither is ever a pass); consumer reader rso/slice001/evidence.py RegistryStore (C-004-T021)
custody.write_access: the registrar only; no cell seat writes
custody.independence_caveat: the registrar is a fleet seat outside the cell, not a separate organisation; custody qualifies byte identity since registration, nothing more (B5.4). Residual (Aporia, v1.0.2 W2): every seat connects as the same Postgres superuser, which can disable the refusal triggers, so write exclusivity is procedural; tampering is DETECTED (chain recompute plus heads Aporia publishes on comms) rather than prevented. Custody QUALIFIED means 'bytes registered at the recorded time, chain intact at check time', within B5.4, and never more
custody.trust_boundary: draft B B5.4: bytes since registration only; never execution, truth or authorship
custody.why_format: exhaustive, sorted; KEEPER_ROW_MISSING:<record_kind> per missing kind

CL-RET(M): OBSERVER(M, o) PASS for every observer o registered as used on M
